steps.title: Cover 1
steps.body: Man coverage with one deep safety in the middle. Everyone else matches a receiver; one defender may sit in the middle as a 'rat' or rush.

steps.title: Cover 0
steps.body: Man coverage with no deep safety. The defense sends an extra rusher or two. Big risk, big pressure: one missed tackle can be a touchdown.

diagram.caption: Cover 0: all-out man, no deep help

steps.prompt: Corners pressed, one safety deep. What coverage is coming?
steps.explanation: Pressed corners and a single deep safety point to Cover 1. After the snap everyone matches up and the free safety stays deep.

steps.prompt: Nobody is deep and linebackers are walked up into the gaps. What's coming?
steps.explanation: No deep safety at all and extra rushers threatening: Cover 0. The answer is a quick throw.

steps.prompt: Against Cover 0, what should the quarterback look for?
choices: A quick throw before the rush arrives
Time to read the whole field
steps.explanation: More rushers than blockers means the ball has to come out fast.

steps.prompt: Which concept is built to beat man coverage?
choices: Mesh: two crossers rubbing past each other
Curl-flat: a curl and a flat route on one side
Smash: a hitch under a corner route
Flood: three routes at three depths on one side
steps.explanation: Crossing routes make man defenders fight through traffic.

steps.title: Cover 2
steps.body: Two safeties split the deep field in halves. The corners squat in the flats and five defenders play zones underneath.

steps.title: The tells
steps.body: Two high safeties wide on the hashes, and corners about 5 yards off with outside leverage, ready to jam and sit in the flat.

steps.title: Where it's weak
steps.body: The deep middle between the safeties, and the sideline behind a squatting corner. Smash, a hitch under a corner route, attacks that corner.

steps.prompt: Two deep safeties on the hashes, corners 5 yards off and outside. What coverage?
steps.explanation: Two wide safeties plus squatting corners: Cover 2. Watch the corners sink into the flats.

steps.prompt: Read this shell, then watch the snap.
steps.explanation: The corners stay short and the safeties take deep halves: Cover 2.

steps.prompt: Smash puts a hitch under a corner route. Why does it beat Cover 2?
choices: The flat corner can't cover both
The safeties can't see the hitch
The corners have to cover the deep middle
steps.explanation: The corner sits on the hitch, the corner route goes over him before the safety arrives.

steps.title: Cover 3
steps.body: The two corners and the free safety each take a deep third. Four defenders play zones underneath, often with the strong safety down near the box.

steps.title: The tells
steps.body: One deep safety in the middle, corners off the ball about 7 yards, and the strong safety rolled down.

steps.title: Where it's weak
steps.body: Four vertical routes against three deep defenders, and the seams. Underneath, curl-flat stretches the outside defender.

steps.prompt: One deep safety, corners 7 yards off, strong safety down. What coverage?
steps.explanation: Off corners with a single-high safety: Cover 3. The corners bail to deep thirds at the snap.

steps.prompt: Name the coverage, then watch it.
steps.explanation: One high, corners off and bailing deep: Cover 3, not Cover 1's pressed man.

steps.prompt: Why do four verticals stress Cover 3?
choices: Four deep routes against three deep defenders
The corners must play man on the slots
The single safety has to blitz
steps.explanation: Three deep defenders can't carry four deep routes, especially up the seams.

steps.title: Cover 4
steps.body: The two corners and two safeties each take a deep quarter. Three defenders play underneath. The safeties also read the slot receivers and fit the run fast.

steps.title: The tells
steps.body: Two safeties, but tighter and shallower than Cover 2, about 10 yards, and corners deeper, about 8 yards.

steps.title: Where it's weak
steps.body: Underneath: with four players deep, quick throws to the flats and curl-flat combinations find room.

steps.prompt: Two safeties about 10 yards deep, corners 8 yards off. What coverage?
steps.explanation: Two safeties tight to the box with deep corners: quarters. All four drop to deep quarters.

steps.prompt: Name it, then watch the snap.
steps.explanation: The corners go deep instead of squatting, and the safeties stay close: Cover 4, not Cover 2.

steps.prompt: Cover 2 and Cover 4 both show two safeties. Which tell separates them?
choices: Corner depth: shallow in Cover 2, deep in Cover 4
The number of linemen in the front
Where the tight end lines up
steps.explanation: Squatting corners at 5 mean Cover 2; corners at 8 with tighter safeties mean quarters.

steps.title: The checklist
steps.body: Count the deep safeties (one or two), check corner depth and leverage, and look for walked-up defenders. Then decide: man or zone, and which shell.

steps.explanation: Pressed corners with one deep safety: Cover 1 man.
Single-high, off corners, strong safety down: Cover 3.
Two wide safeties and squatting corners: Cover 2.
No deep safety and linebackers in the gaps: Cover 0. Get the ball out.

steps.prompt: Match each coverage to a concept that attacks it.
steps.explanation: Each coverage leaves a weakness: the deep middle or corner in Cover 2, the seams in Cover 3, underneath in Cover 4, crossing traffic in man.
